items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: "I want you to meet Mr. René, Mr. Leon Renéey."

ctx.x: Leon and Otis René, were very marvelous musicians, song writers. And very successful, very successful. They did, "Sleepy Time Down South," and they did -- in later years Leon, I think -- I don't know if the both of them wrote it, but I know Leon wrote Swallows, "When the Swallows Come Back to Capistrano," and many other things, marvelous things. And I remember my aunt, Augusta Glover, who was my husband's aunt,

really, well, she was a very close friend to the Renéys, and she admired them greatly, and they lived in her neighborhood. She happened to have been a dear friend to Leon's wife. They worked at PTAs and things together, and they later got me involved in all of that also. But anyway, my aunt said to me, she says, "You know, I'm -- I want Mr. René, I want you to meet Mr. René, Mr. Leon Renéey." So they lived --
